## In-seat review of record — `domain:ui` @ objectui

Claim declared `Clause-②: no`, and that still holds after reading the diff: nothing new becomes authorable, no published declaration moves, and the accept set is byte-identical. What changed is a **fallback**.

### ⭐ My ZONE 2 A was wrong, and being wrong there is the whole value of this PR

I handed over: *"the caller-supplied `header` is always the raw field name, so replacing it with a humanized label is always an improvement"* — flagged as the item I most expected to bite, and it did. The census found what my guess missed: `normalizeColumns` folds the spec-canonical `{ field, label }` **and** the adapter-canonical `{ accessorKey, header }` onto the same `col.header` (objectui#5351), and `DashboardRenderer` forwards an authored widget's `columns` here verbatim. ⇒ a genuine author-written label arrives on **exactly the key an unconditional humanize would overwrite.**

⭐ And it was not argued, it was **measured against the repair itself**: ablation leg 2 makes the fallback unconditional and turns the two AUTHORED LABEL assertions red while every PARITY assertion stays green. ⇒ the unconditional version **satisfies the card as written** and silently discards an author's label — trading this defect for a strictly worse one. That is the single most useful thing in this PR, and a dev that had merely done what the brief said would have shipped it.

### What I verified myself

- ✅ **`ObjectChart.tsx` is absent from the diff**, as ruling 3 required — it was in the merge queue under objectui#9037 while this was being written. Three files changed, none of them a call site.
- ✅ **The repair is in the whitelist branch**, beside the asymmetry it has to match, not at the two callers.
- ⭐ **Reference preservation is not incidental.** `return header === col.header ? col : { ...col, header }` keeps unchanged entries **by reference**, citing objectui#4618's data-table column-state re-seed. ⚠️ Worth flagging up: objectui#8640 is an **open decision card** asking when objectui code may depend on the identity of a memo result, and this is a live instance answering it correctly by hand. Not a defect — a data point for that card.
- ⚠️ **One deliberate behaviour change the PR body should not bury.** The old code short-circuited on `!objectName` and returned `normalized` untouched; the new code still humanizes in that case. ⇒ a standalone `object-data-table` (no `objectName`) with `{ accessorKey: 'close_date', header: 'close_date' }` now renders `Close Date` where it rendered `close_date`. The report **does** account for this — it is the "fourth population" — and it is the right answer, because the auto-derive branch humanizes regardless of `objectName`. I am naming it because it is the one movement a reader of the diff could miss.

### On the condition's one genuine ambiguity

`col.header !== col.accessorKey` cannot distinguish *"the drill caller stamped the raw key"* from *"an author deliberately wants the raw key shown."* That ambiguity is inherent, and the PR resolves it the right way for a reason stronger than "the drill case is commoner": **a bare-string column was already humanized by `normalizeColumns` on the way in**, so `columns: ['close_date']` has always rendered `Close Date`. ⇒ making the object form agree is **restoring consistency between two spellings of the same authoring**, not imposing a new opinion. That argument is in the report and it is the correct one.

### Corrections to the card the PR makes

- **Three drill surfaces move, not four.** `ObjectPivotTable`, `ObjectMetricWidget` and `ObjectChart` pass a whitelist; the filer's fourth (`DatasetWidget`) and app-shell's `ReportView` render the drawer with **no** `columns` prop, so their headers were already auto-derived. ⇒ lane fact ⑰ again — a card's own member list is a claim, not a census.
- **The branch was never uniformly broken.** Only the OBJECT form carried the raw key through — which is exactly the form both drill callers construct. A sharper statement of the defect than the card's.
- ZONE 2 D held **by half**: `DrillDownDrawer.tsx:122` is still accurate; `ObjectChart.tsx:1388` is stale (the map is at 1399). ⇒ "stale by default" is a prior, not a law — the diff correctly cites no line either way.

### Verdict

**Approved — land on all-checks-green.** ⛔ Not armed while any check is outstanding. Successor objectui#9055 (two more field-key display spellings, including `resolveSeriesLabel` falling back to the raw y-field key — the same fallback shape this PR removes) is correctly a card and not a passenger.

## ⚠️ `Test (shard 2/4)` is red, and it is **not** this PR's failure — one re-run spent

Recording the reasoning rather than just re-running, because "flake" is not a root cause and this one now has a history.

### The failure

```
FAIL packages/plugin-grid/src/__tests__/formatHintedColumnRenderer-8920.test.tsx
  > objectui#8920 — every ObjectGrid path honours a `format` hint
  > P: compound-cell prefix badge still draws the select renderer (must-not-change pin)

AssertionError: expected [] to include 'tel:+15551234567'
  ❯ formatHintedColumnRenderer-8920.test.tsx:262:33
```

Everything else is green: 734 files passed, 9639 tests, one failure.

### Why it is not this PR's

1. **The diff does not touch `plugin-grid`.** Three files changed: `ObjectDataTable.tsx`, its new pin, and a changeset — all `plugin-dashboard`. There is no path from this change to that renderer.
2. **This is a known, already-filed flake: objectui#9035**, filed by this seat earlier today with the mechanism diagnosed. The assertion at `:262` is the only one in that block **not** wrapped in `waitFor`:
   ```ts
   await waitFor(() => expect(screen.getByText('Alice')).toBeInTheDocument());
   await waitFor(() => expect(container.textContent).toContain('New'));
   expect(telHrefs(container)).toContain(`tel:${HINTED_PHONE}`);   // ← no wait of its own
   ```
3. **`expected []` is the tell.** An empty collection in the failure message means the render had not settled — not that the renderer is broken. If the hinted column were genuinely un-promoted, `telHrefs` would return the *other* hrefs, not nothing. This lane records that as a standing fact precisely so a real defect is not mistaken for this.

⇒ ⛔ Not diagnosed as "flaky, retry" — diagnosed as a **specific missing `await`** in a test the diff does not touch.

### What I did, and what I did not

- ✅ **One re-run of the failed job, and that is the only one.** Per this lane's rule a re-run confirms a not-this-PR reading; it is not a strategy. If shard 2 comes back red on the same commit, the reading is wrong and the failure becomes this PR's to root-cause.
- ⛔ **Did not touch the test.** It belongs to objectui#9035 and to `plugin-grid`; repairing it here would widen a `plugin-dashboard` PR into another package to go green, which is the move that turns a clean diff into an unreviewable one.
- ⛔ **Did not skip, disable or quarantine anything.**

### ⚠️ Escalating the cost, because it is now measurable

This is the **second** PR this session to lose a CI cycle to objectui#9035 — objectui#9028 hit the identical assertion earlier and also came back green on one re-run of the same commit. ⇒ a `priority:p3` test-hygiene card is levying a recurring tax on unrelated lanes, and the fix is one `waitFor`. This seat is raising its practical priority in the queue; the grade itself remains the triage seat's.

The in-seat review above stands: **approved, land on green.**
